name: cmux.terminal.connector/1
docs: Host mode (ghostty-next-switch.md, cloud-app.md): the far end runs its own session host; the local host relays the viewer protocol (GHOSTSNP snapshot plus bytes, size state, input, presence) and does not parse. An app connector runs as the app's server (implements with server: true) and needs the restricted scope terminal:backend. Rust trait TerminalConnector.

methods.connect: ({kind, target, open_token}) -> {channel, window_bytes}: a viewer-protocol byte stream the local host relays; a kind not in options.kinds fails with denied

kinds.description: Target kinds this implementation serves; the registry ids are app:<app>/<kind>. Default deny: a kind not listed is never routed here.

status: draft: shapes chosen by the ghostty-next lead (2026-10-04); refined with the first connector before the interface is public; 2026-10-04: credit-based data frames shared with cmux.terminal.backend/1

eventShapes.end: end {channel, lost: {reason, retryable}} after the last data

dataPlane.frames: Data moves as frames on the app host's stream (binary payload), never as op calls. Per channel, in order: data {channel, offset, bytes} (offset = running byte total after this frame, per direction), credit {channel, direction: in|out, bytes} and end {channel, exit? | lost?} (exactly once, after the last data). channel is the connector link; the bytes are the viewer protocol (GHOSTSNP snapshot and terminal bytes frames, size state, input, presence).
dataPlane.credit: The receiver grants bytes; the sender keeps at most the granted, not yet acknowledged bytes in flight and never sends past them. Each direction starts with window_bytes (from the open answer, 64 KiB to 1 MiB, default 256 KiB); the receiver sends credit as it consumes data. Data past the credit is a protocol violation: the receiver ends the channel with lost {reason: "credit", retryable: false}. No frame or op waits.
dataPlane.backpressure: End to end: the session host grants output credit for a terminal only while its viewers and journal keep up; a backend grants host-channel out credit only from its own terminal credit, so a slow viewer stops the far end (SSH window) instead of growing a buffer. Input runs the other way the same way.
dataPlane.continuity: A receiver checks offsets: a gap or an overlap ends the channel with lost. resume continues the offsets of the resumed terminal.
